land.text: Edom 'conquered by Nabonidus in the 6th century BC' (infobox c. 553 BC)

successors.note: The Edom page also says the kingdom was destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar II in 587/86 BC. The Nabataeans 'had already established their own kingdom in what used to be Edom by the first half of the 2nd century BC' (Cliopatria's Nabataeans begin in -164), and a 'truncated province of Idumea' is attested by 365.

capitals.name: Bozrah (Buseirah)
capitals.note: 'The ancient capital of Edom was Bozrah.' The page gives no coordinates; the dot is at the modern site of Buseirah near Tafilah, approximate.

correction.text: the land of Seir: the Edomite plateau around Bozrah and the Arabah with Faynan ('1300-800 BC'), the Ma'an desert east of 36.4 E left out

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Edom (its Neo-Assyrian shape of -700 and the Achaemenid and Nabataean shapes contain the land). The page gives no area and no boundary; it names Seir, Bozrah, Teman, the Arabah (Faynan) and, in Amaziah's time, the seaports of Eilat and Ezion-Geber, and says Edomites settled 'parts of the Negev down to Timna' before 587/86. The shape is the gazetteer's Edom region (Tafilah, Ma'an, Aqaba governorates) cut at 36.4 E, about 20,000 km2: a reading, not a border. The Negev and Eilat are not included.

region.text: the land of Seir: the Edomite plateau around Bozrah and the Arabah with Faynan ('1300-800 BC'), the Ma'an desert east of 36.4 E left out

ledger.note: c. 1215 BC: Edom appears in the record. Infobox 'Established: c. 13th century BC'; the page cites 'the list of the Egyptian pharaoh Seti I from c. 1215 BC' as the earliest mention and says the nation 'flourished between the 13th and the 8th centuries BC'. It names no founder.

region.text: the land of Seir: the Edomite plateau around Bozrah and the Arabah with Faynan ('1300-800 BC'), the Ma'an desert east of 36.4 E left out

ledger.note: 734 BC: Edom pays tribute to Assyria. 'Asqaluna, Judah, Edom, Moab and Ammon, and the Mu'na Arab tribe, all began paying tribute to Tiglath-Pileser' in the campaign of 734; the Edom page names Kaus-malaka 'at the time of Tiglath-pileser III (c. 745 BC)', Aya-ramu 'at the time of Sennacherib (c. 705 BC)', Kaus-gabri 'at the time of Esarhaddon (c. 680 BC)' and an Assyrian inscription of 667 BC without calling them vassals.

region.text: the land of Seir: the Edomite plateau around Bozrah and the Arabah with Faynan ('1300-800 BC'), the Ma'an desert east of 36.4 E left out

ledger.note: c. 609 BCE (bridged): Assyria's overlordship ends. No page opened dates when Edom stopped paying Assyria; the year mirrors the neo-assyrian-empire dossier's close of the 734 tributaries.

region.text: the land of Seir: the Edomite plateau around Bozrah and the Arabah with Faynan ('1300-800 BC'), the Ma'an desert east of 36.4 E left out

ledger.note: c. 609 BCE (bridged): Edom is under Babylon. The Nebuchadnezzar page has the kings of Ammon, Edom, Moab, Sidon and Tyre meeting at Jerusalem in 594 BC to discuss throwing off Babylonian control; the start of Babylonian overlordship is undated. [Reviewer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: year moved from -609 to -605: the Nebuchadnezzar II page says the victory at Carchemish in 605 BC 'resulted in all of Syria and Israel coming under the control of the Neo-Babylonian Empire' and puts no Babylonian overlordship in the Levant before 605; 609 is the fall of Harran, not Babylon's arrival.]

region.text: the land of Seir: the Edomite plateau around Bozrah and the Arabah with Faynan ('1300-800 BC'), the Ma'an desert east of 36.4 E left out

ledger.note: 587 BC: Edom rebels against Babylon. 'In 587 BC, Ammon, Edom and Moab likewise rebelled'; the Edom page adds 'the destruction of the kingdom by Nebuchadnezzar II in 587/86 BC' and that Edomites 'may have helped plunder Jerusalem'. The outcome for Edom's independence is contradictory: the infobox ends the state in c. 553 BC.

region.text: the land of Seir: the Edomite plateau around Bozrah and the Arabah with Faynan ('1300-800 BC'), the Ma'an desert east of 36.4 E left out

ledger.note: 553 BC: Nabonidus takes Edom. 'After a period of illness, Nabonidus then moved on Amurru and Edom and captured an otherwise unknown city' in the campaign that began 'In May 553 BC'; the Edom page: 'Edom ceased to exist as a state when it was conquered by Nabonidus in the 6th century BC' (infobox c. 553 BC). The page does not date the move on Edom within the campaign.

region.text: the land of Seir: the Edomite plateau around Bozrah and the Arabah with Faynan ('1300-800 BC'), the Ma'an desert east of 36.4 E left out

ledger.note: c. 553 BC: the Kingdom of Edom ends. Infobox end c. 553 BC; the Nabataeans later 'established their own kingdom in what used to be Edom by the first half of the 2nd century BC' and 'truncated province of Idumea' is attested by 365.

wars.name: Saul's war against Edom
wars.outcome: The page mentions 'their defeat by King Saul of Israel in the late 11th century BC'; no territorial result is dated.
wars.note: The year -1010 is a placeholder inside the late 11th century. The Israel dossier (me-04-a) has Edom as David's client c. 1000-930 (bridged); the Edom page says only that the Edomite prince Hadad fled to Egypt and returned 'after David's death' (undated).

wars.name: Amaziah of Judah's war against Edom

zones.text: 'Eilat and Ezion-Geber its seaports', said to be under Amaziah's time (796-769 BC)

wars.outcome: Amaziah 'defeated Edom'; the Red Sea ports of Eilat and Ezion-Geber are said to be Judah's 'under Amaziah's time (796-769 BC)'.
wars.note: The span is Amaziah's reign; the page gives no year for the battle. Not drawn in the ledger because no year and no change of owner are dated; a gap-filler should open 'Amaziah of Judah'.

wars.name: Revolt of Ammon, Edom and Moab against Nebuchadnezzar II
wars.outcome: 'In 587 BC, Ammon, Edom and Moab likewise rebelled'; the Edom page puts the 'destruction of the kingdom by Nebuchadnezzar II in 587/86 BC'.
wars.note: The infobox ends the state in c. 553 BC, which is used here.

wars.name: Nabonidus's Arabian campaign

zones.text: the land of Seir: the Edomite plateau around Bozrah and the Arabah with Faynan ('1300-800 BC'), the Ma'an desert east of 36.4 E left out

wars.outcome: Edom captured in 553 BC; Nabonidus then fights the king of Dadanu and takes Tayma, where he lives in exile from 552 to 543/542 BC.
wars.note: 'In May 553 BC, Nabonidus departed to campaign in Arabia'; his reign is 25 May 556 - 13 October 539 BC.

certainty.note: No Edomite boundary is described on any page opened; the plateau, the Arabah and the Negev settlements are named only as places.

notes: Cliopatria has no Edom; its Neo-Assyrian (-700), Achaemenid and Nabataean shapes contain the same land as direct imperial or Nabataean territory. The Edom page contradicts itself on the end: 'destruction of the kingdom by Nebuchadnezzar II in 587/86 BC' against 'conquered by Nabonidus' (infobox c. 553 BC); this dossier uses 553 and treats 587 as the rebellion. Judah's control (Jehoshaphat c. 870-849, Amaziah 796-769) is not drawn: the page dates neither a conquest nor a loss, and a gap-filler should open 'Amaziah of Judah' and 'Jehoram of Judah'. David's overlordship is carried in the kingdom-of-israel dossier only. The Idumea of the Persian and Hellenistic periods (province by 365, Judean conquest c. 163 BC) and the Nabataean takeover are outside the dossier's span; the 553-164 interval is a Babylonian then Persian province with no state of its own, so the renderer should hand the land to the Achaemenid dossier (me-05) and to the nabataeans dossier. The polygon in the keyframe only cuts the Ma'an desert off the gazetteer's Edom region.
